candidates.title: Diffusion-enhanced GFlowNet for solving vehicle routing problems
candidates.abstract: Traditional neural solvers for solving vehicle routing problems (VRPs) often suffer from limited solution diversity, motivating the development of Generative Flow Network (GFlowNet)-based models.However, the effectiveness of these models is frequently constrained by insufficient flow expansion in high-reward regions, limiting their ability to distribute probability across promising solution routes.The deeper exploration could yield superior results.Diffusion models, in contrast, provide stronger structural guidance for exploration.These two paradigms are naturally complementary: GFlowNet can supply edge-level signals for diffusion to embed, while diffusion can guide broader exploration.Leveraging this synergy, we propose Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet (DEG), a novel framework that integrates GFlowNet with a diffusion model to encourage richer flow expansion toward highreward regions and derive higher-quality solutions.Specifically, DEG exploits GFlowNet's inherent diversity to generate edge-specific backward signals, applies the stochastic noise schedule of diffusion to perturb these signals, and then denoises them within the GFlowNet paradigm.To further improve scalability, we introduce a specialized decoder capable of dynamically adapting to diverse problem scales.Extensive experimental evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, including instances with up to 10,000 nodes, demonstrate that DEG consistently achieves favorable performance compared to baseline methods.The code is available at https://github.com/ZHANG-NI/DEG.Recent neural solvers for VRPs can be broadly categorized into Autoregressive (AR) and Non-Autoregressive (NAR) models.AR models, such as those based on pointer networks and Transformer 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026).

candidates.title: Optimal-transport flow matching for stochastic model ipdating
candidates.abstract: Deep generative models have attracted considerable attention as inference engines for stochastic model updating. Among these deep generative models, conditional flow matching offers a particularly efficient formulation, in which a continuous transport map from a latent distribution to the posterior is learned by regression against optimal-transport probability paths, avoiding both the invertibility constraints of normalising flows and the iterative denoising of diffusion models. However, its performance in engineering model updating has not been examined against an established baseline such as the Bayesian updating framework under controlled conditions. In this work, conditional flow matching is therefore assessed against the Bayesian model updating approach with transitional Markov chain Monte Carlo, in which the Bhattacharyya distance provides the approximate likelihood for the Bayesian approach. The two methods are assessed with respect to posterior fidelity, evaluated by statistical distances against the known ground truth and computational expenditure in model evaluations, with the offline training budget reported separately from the inference cost of each subsequent conditioning. A 3-DOF spring–mass system with uncertain stiffness parameters serves as the benchmark. Since the calibrated posterior constitutes the input description upon which subsequent reliability assessment depends, the accuracy and the marginal cost of the updating step both bear directly on reliability computations. In addition, the amortised nature of the learned transport map is discussed in this work, as it permits the posterior to be re-evaluated under new observations at negligible cost, which is a property of practical relevance to reliability assessment under sequentially acquired monitoring data.

candidates.title: DockBind: A Quality-Controlled Data Set of Modeled Protein-Ligand Complexes Associated with Affinity Data.
candidates.abstract: Ligand-protein interaction prediction is essential for structure-based drug discovery, but further development of machine-learning scoring functions is limited by a lack of high-quality training data sets. Here, we present DockBind, a curated data set of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, generated through a quality-controlled docking workflow. This workflow was developed based on an expanded docking benchmark, where we systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods as well as ligand similarity and maximum common substructure (MCS)-based pose filtering to generate and identify the most realistic poses. The resulting workflow was then incorporated into a pipeline integrating structural and binding affinity data from Binding MOAD, the Protein Data Bank, ChEMBL, and BindingDB, which resulted in 18,332 complexes across 612 protein targets, with high structural reliability and chemical diversity─the DockBind data set─providing a valuable resource for training and benchmarking machine-learning scoring functions.

candidates.title: Design of a multi-stage hybrid optimizer combining Bayesian and evolutionary algorithms for modeling and optimizing seizure-related information in EEG signals
candidates.abstract: The prediction of epileptic seizures from EEG signal analysis is modeled as a complex, high-dimensional, multi-objective optimization problem. In this study, we propose and design a novel multi-stage hybrid optimizer that integrates Bayesian optimization with a family of evolutionary and metaheuristic algorithms, including Genetic Algorithm (GA), Evolutionary Programming (EP), Evolution Strategies (ES), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), and Harmony Search (HS).This optimizer is structured to operate across sequential stages of optimization, where each stage is designed to progressively refine the solution space by selecting the optimal subset of EEG channels and time blocks related to the preictal phase. The mathematical model aims to maximize the posterior probability of seizure occurrence while minimizing the temporal distance to the actual seizure, thus formulating a well-defined trade-off in the objective space. Unlike traditional methods, the proposed hybrid framework models and controls the optimization trajectory by combining the global exploration capability of evolutionary algorithms with the adaptive search of Bayesian optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimizer successfully converges toward high-informational regions of EEG data that occur early in the preictal phase. A detailed performance comparison and sensitivity analysis further validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach, offering insights into the design of more generalizable hybrid optimizers for complex modeling tasks.

candidates.title: Benchmarking and Experimental Validation of Machine Learning Strategies for Enzyme Engineering.
candidates.abstract: Enzyme-directed evolution increasingly relies on computational tools to prioritize mutations, yet their practical value is difficult to assess because kinetic data are often aggregated across heterogeneous assay conditions, inflating apparent generalization. Here we introduce EnzyArena, a curated benchmark in which kinetic parameters (kcat, Km, or kcat/Km) are grouped by experimental campaign and measured under matched conditions, thereby minimizing confounders such as pH, temperature, reaction, and batch. Using EnzyArena, we systematically evaluate 20 models spanning four widely used strategies for guiding enzyme evolution: protein-ligand binding affinity prediction, protein stability prediction, zero-shot fitness prediction and enzyme kinetic parameters prediction. Across subsets derived from public databases and 25 literature-derived mutagenesis data sets, most models exhibit weak, fragile, or inconsistent correlation with measured functional outcomes. Kinetic-parameter predictors perform strongly on database-derived subsets but lose their advantage on literature-derived mutagenesis data sets, whereas zero-shot predictors show more consistent generalization. A simple consensus of multiple zero-shot models further improves the precision of identifying beneficial mutants in retrospective analyses. We prospectively validated these findings in a wet-lab campaign (150 mutants) comparing random mutants, UniKP-prioritized mutants, and ESM-1v-prioritized mutants (representing supervised kinetic parameters prediction and zero-shot fitness prediction, respectively), where ESM-1v achieved the highest utility and UniKP underperformed the random baseline. Together, this study establishes realistic baselines for computational mutant prioritization and indicates that zero-shot strategies provide the most consistent, although still modest, performance among the approaches evaluated.

candidates.title: Multi-Objective Constrained Deep Q-Networks for Supplier Selection and Order Allocation in Sustainable Supply Chains
candidates.abstract: Abstract Sustainable sourcing requires sequential decisions that couple discrete supplier admission, integer order quantities, stochastic lead times, inventory, and competing economic, environmental, and service objectives. We formulate this setting as a preference-conditioned constrained Markov decision process with state-dependent, mixed-integer action feasibility and distributional tail-risk requirements. We develop ParetoShield-Q, a multi-objective deep Q-learning formulation that uses an augmented Chebyshev action functional over distributional cost-to-go estimates and a completion-feasibility oracle to construct executable supplier allocations. The same constrained Bellman operator jointly determines which objectives are optimized, which downstream risks are penalized, and which supplier--quantity assignments are legally selectable. We establish conditional one-step feasibility and finite-candidate Pareto-efficiency properties, and provide an evaluation protocol based on the public M5 demand data and a public supplier-attribute dataset. The study presents seven quantitative tables and eight vector figures spanning multi-objective performance, preference control, cost composition, operational feasibility, ablations, disruption response, and computational scaling. The visualizations reproduce the tabulated numerical summaries without constructing unobserved run-level training traces. Independent reproduction requires the source training runs, scenario configurations, and optimizer logs.

candidates.title: Shedding Light: A Benchmark for Evaluating Lighting Understanding in Generative Image Models
candidates.abstract: Accurate modelling of illumination is central to realistic image synthesis and scene understanding. Yet, there is little exploration into whether image generative models are good at this task or whether physical plausibility remains a key challenge for them. Clearly, significant progress has been made in realistic image synthesis, but do models truly understand lighting in a physically accurate manner? To answer this question, this work proposes a benchmark to assess the lighting understanding and harmonisation capabilities of generative models. Our key insight is that evaluating lighting understanding for such models only requires testing how well they insert novel objects into real photographs whilst maintaining consistent illumination. To do so, we use a multi-illumination dataset with images containing simple objects serving as "light probes", and prompt models to inpaint the same object onto the original image, then compare the generated results against the ground-truth light probes. We then estimate the lighting direction, colour and radiance distribution from the inpainted probes, providing a quantitative measure of illumination accuracy and photometric realism. Our work establishes a scalable evaluation protocol to systematically assess how well generative models capture and reproduce real-world lighting, offering a foundation for benchmarking the photometric accuracy of any future models. All code and data are available at https://lvsn.github.io/SheddingLight/.

candidates.title: The Energy Landscape of DNA-Binding Proteins Along the Genome
candidates.abstract: Abstract Reconstructing the energy profile of DNA-binding proteins along the genome requires an algorithm that quantifies efficiently the binding free energy. We assembled a dataset of protein structures and DNA binding sites, together with their binding energies, and used it to train a machine-learning algorithm that learns a latent invariant representation of the protein interface and of the DNA sequence, combining them to predict the free energy. After validating the method, we used it to determine the energy profile of a single-domain transcription factor (PU.1) sliding on mammalian chromosomes, predicting its binding regions and quantifying the statistical properties that determine their stability and their kinetic accessibility.

candidates.title: An Intelligent Multi-objective Decision Support Model for Sustainable Remanufacturing
candidates.abstract: Remanufacturing offers small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) viable pathways towards transitioning to a circular economy; however, intelligent decision-making systems are needed to accelerate its adoption. Balancing the economic, environmental, and social dimensions of sustainability requires the use of analytical tools that can handle multi-dimensional complexity. This study presents a multi-objective optimization model where remanufacturing tasks are allocated to machines in a factory on the basis of minimizing costs, emissions, and noise exposure. Tri-objective optimization has been carried out using the quadrant shrinking method, and Pareto optimal solutions are translated to an implementation framework that can equip SMEs with an intelligent tool for circular economy adoption. In addition to this, we propose an implementation framework for circular economy in manufacturing based on the DMAIC (define, measure, analyze, improve, and control) approach.

candidates.title: Women who shaped macromolecular NMR: four decades of innovation in structure, dynamics, membrane proteins, RNA, chromatin, and cellular biophysics
candidates.abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is a uniquely powerful biophysical technique that enables the characterization of biomolecular structure, dynamics, and interactions at atomic resolution under conditions that closely approximate the native cellular environment. Its impact on modern molecular biology and biophysics is difficult to overstate, as it has provided fundamental insights into the molecular principles that govern biological function. In this review, I highlight the remarkable contributions of women scientists to the development and application of macromolecular NMR. Although these contributions have been instrumental in advancing the field, they have often received less recognition than they deserve. By tracing the evolution of biomolecular NMR over the past four decades, I aim to showcase the pioneering work of women researchers whose innovations have shaped many of the major areas of modern macromolecular NMR. The review begins with the foundational advances that established contemporary biomolecular NMR in the 1980s and 1990s, progresses through methodological developments that expanded our understanding of molecular dynamics and intrinsically disordered systems, and concludes with landmark applications that transformed our understanding of diverse biological processes and systems. Importantly, this review is not intended to provide a comprehensive historical account of all women who have contributed to the field or to discuss all their accomplishments. Rather, it reflects a very personal perspective on a selection of particularly influential and inspiring scientists whose work has had a profound impact on macromolecular NMR and its applications to biological research.

candidates.title: The Transformation of Oncology Drug Development in China: Toward a New Phase of Innovation
candidates.abstract: China's oncology drug development ecosystem has shifted from rapid pipeline expansion toward clinical value-driven innovation. We review regulatory reform and the 2015 to 2025 evolution of clinical development across small molecules, mAbs, multispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and cell and gene therapies. China's disease burden and enrollment capacity have enabled globally relevant advances in EGFR-mutant lung cancer, gastrointestinal malignancies, hepatocellular carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and CLDN18.2-directed therapies. We highlight persistent challenges in target and modality convergence, biomarker definition, therapeutic window optimization, manufacturing consistency, and globally interpretable evidence generation and discuss how artificial intelligence may connect target discovery, drug design, and clinical trial optimization more efficiently. SIGNIFICANCE: China has become a major source of oncology trials and modality innovation, but scale alone will not ensure global impact. This review links regulatory reform, disease-specific opportunity, target biology, therapeutic format, and evidence quality across a decade of solid tumor development. It defines the conditions under which China-originated programs can generate globally practice-changing evidence. See related article by Shi, p. XX .

candidates.title: Investigation and Optimization of Air Pollution Risk by a Multi-criteria Decision Making Method Using Fuzzy TOPSIS: A Case Study of Construction Workers
candidates.abstract: Background: Investigating human health during work importantly affect the safety and efficiency of the society. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. However, among the sub-criteria, the most effective ones were “worker knowledge”, “manager knowledge”, “logistic specialized managers”, “modern facilities”, and “modern technology”. The selection of the linear and non-linear models was conducted according to the F values, and the model parameters were estimated using the Newton-Raphson test. Most coefficients were significant at P= 0.99. The model also has a high describing value of 0.97. The final estimated homogeneity coefficient was equal to 1.31, and it ranged from 0.86 to 2.72 for the critical risk investigation. The significance of the present research is to increase the health and safety of workers during work resulting in a more sustainable and healthier environment. Conclusion: Accordingly, the managers could handle the risks, determine the tolerable risks, indicate the risk of each process to control expenses, and take the essential measures for optimization.

candidates.title: Fast Solution Methods for the Classical 0–1 Knapsack Problem
candidates.abstract: The classical 0--1 knapsack problem is among the simplest integer programs to state and among the most instructive problems for understanding why algorithm selection must follow instance structure. An input contains items with positive integer weights and profits, and the task is to choose a maximum-profit subset whose total weight does not exceed a capacity. The problem is weakly NP-hard, yet many large instances are solved quickly because exact algorithms exploit moderate numeric parameters, strong linear relaxations, dominance relations, or a small set of uncertain variables near the fractional break item. This review develops a theory-guided account of the principal fast solution methods for the classical problem. It proves the correctness and complexity of weight-indexed and profit-indexed dynamic programming, explains sparse Pareto-frontier implementations and reconstruction, derives the fractional-knapsack upper bound used by branch-and-bound methods, and establishes the correctness of meet-in-the-middle search. It then presents the core concept that underlies influential practical solvers and gives a detailed proof of the standard profit-scaling fully polynomial-time approximation scheme. Modern advances based on structured min-plus convolution are placed within this classical landscape rather than treated as isolated results. The central conclusion is that there is no universally fastest knapsack algorithm. Small item counts favor meet-in-the-middle search, moderate capacities or total profits favor dynamic programming, favorable density structure favors core-based exact methods, and very large numeric coefficients favor approximation. A final decision framework translates these theoretical distinctions into an implementable solver-selection policy while identifying open questions concerning adaptivity, certified switching among methods, memory efficiency, and realistic hard-instance generation.

candidates.title: CoatFusion: Controllable Material Coating in Images
candidates.abstract: Material Coating is a novel image editing task that simulates applying a thin material layer to a target surface (substrate) while preserving the substrate's geometry and shading. Material coating is fundamentally different from material transfer, which typically reinterprets an object as being made of a new material and can modify its shape or overwrite fine details. We introduce CoatFusion , a diffusion-based framework for controllable material coating in images. Since real paired before/after coating data is difficult to acquire, we construct DataCoat110K , a synthetic paired dataset of approximately 110K examples rendered with physically motivated coating layers, including opaque, metallic, and transmissive appearances. CoatFusion formulates coating as visual in-context learning over a triptych containing the substrate image, a canonical 2D albedo texture, and the coated result, and uses cycle-consistent compose/decompose supervision to encourage substrate preservation and geometry-aware texture wrapping. Learned material tokens provide continuous control over roughness and thickness, and discrete on/off control over metalness and transmission. Across held-out synthetic evaluations, real-image examples, ablations, and a human study, CoatFusion produces more realistic and controllable coatings than material transfer/editing baselines and classical blending operations. Code and data for this paper are available at https://github.com/sagielevy/coatFusion.

candidates.title: Multi-Enzyme Data-Independent Acquisition Mass Spectrometry for Proteoform-Aware Single-shot Proteomics
candidates.abstract: Biological regulation does not operate at the level of the protein but across ensembles of protein variants shaped by alternative splicing, post-translational modification and endogenous proteolytic processing. Yet most conventional bottom-up discovery proteomics workflows remain optimized for a canonical protein census, leaving much of the sequence-level variation invisible. Multi-enzyme digestion has been recognized as an effective strategy to expand sequence coverage and proteoform sensitivity, but existing implementations rely on resource-heavy per-enzyme liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis, dedicated measurements for spectral library construction, and semi-manual reconciliation across multiple software tools, restricting the use to specialized laboratories and limited sample cohorts. Here we introduce mE-DIA, a multi-enzyme, proteoform-resolved data independent acquisition (DIA)-MS workflow that multiplexes complementary protease digested samples into a single DIA injection and processes them through a library-free pipeline within a single analysis engine, without supplemental data dependent acquisition (DDA)-MS measurements. The mE-DIA Pipeline graphical user interface orchestrates the analysis, and a dedicated proteoform inference algorithm and the interactive mE-DIA Peptide Mapper viewer make the sequence-level evidence explorable. Comparing the workflow to prevailing DDA-library-based multi-enzyme DIA on the same raw data and within shared search space showed increased identified protein groups by 30 % and protein groups quantified at [≤] 20 % CV by 47 %. A three-enzyme multiplex of the human pathogen Streptococcus pyogenes resolved 990 protein-backbone variants among 309 canonical protein entries, 1.8-fold more than the most productive single-enzyme analysis, including an H69 C-terminal proteoform of the ribosomal protein uS19 that the trypsin-only workflow did not resolve. By consolidating multi-enzyme acquisition, analysis and proteoform interpretation into one accessible toolset, mE-DIA brings sub-gene-resolved evidence within reach of routine single-shot discovery DIA proteomics.

candidates.title: A physically integrated GNN surrogate for microbially-mediated kinetic reactive transport: PHYGNET
candidates.abstract: Abstract. Reactive transport modelling (RTM) is essential for subsurface environmental management but is fundamentally constrained by traditional geochemical solvers. These solvers incur prohibitive computational costs and frequently suffer from numerical instabilities such as convergence failures, particularly in microbially-mediated kinetic reaction systems. While machine learning surrogates offer acceleration, they often lack physical consistency when dealing with stiff biogeochemical dynamics. Here we propose PHYGNET (Physically GNN Network), which maps microbial reaction networks into a directed graph by representing species and reactions as nodes and edges. It embeds Monod-type kinetics within a physics layer to enforce mass conservation and thermodynamic hierarchies, and incorporates a residual corrector for refinement. By successfully coupling with COMSOL, PHYGNET demonstrates the capability to execute full reactive transport simulations. Benchmark tests reveal that, in contrast to the severe super-linear time penalties faced by traditional solvers at engineering scales, PHYGNET maintains stable sub-linear scaling via tensor parallelism. At a scale of 105 grid nodes, PHYGNET achieved an acceleration (up to 3524-fold) without numerical crashes. Furthermore, its escalating speedup ratio establishes a "small-sample training, ultra-large-scale inference" paradigm that effectively offsets initial data generation costs. Overall, PHYGNET provides an efficient and physically consistent framework for accelerating Monod-type microbial reactive transport simulations, offering a practical pathway for large-scale environmental applications.

candidates.title: Deep operator networks for surrogate modeling of cyclic adsorption processes with varying initial conditions
candidates.abstract: Deep Operator Networks are emerging as fundamental tools among various neural network types to learn mappings between function spaces, and have recently gained attention due to their ability to approximate nonlinear operators. In particular, DeepONets offer a natural formulation for PDE solving, since the solution of a partial differential equation can be interpreted as an operator mapping an initial condition to its corresponding solution field. In this work, we applied DeepONets in the context of process modeling for adsorption technologies, to assess their feasibility as surrogates for cyclic adsorption process simulation and optimization. The goal is to accelerate convergence of cyclic processes such as Temperature-Vacuum Swing Adsorption (TVSA), which require repeated solution of transient PDEs, which are computationally expensive. Since each step of a cyclic adsorption process starts from the final state of the preceding step, effective surrogate modeling requires generalization across a wide range of initial conditions. The governing equations exhibit steep traveling fronts, providing a demanding benchmark for operator learning. To evaluate functional generalization under these conditions, we construct a mixed training dataset composed of heterogeneous initial conditions and train DeepONets to approximate the corresponding solution operators. The trained models are then tested on initial conditions outside the parameter ranges used during training, as well as on completely unseen functional forms. The results demonstrate accurate predictions both within and beyond the training distribution, highlighting DeepONets as potentially efficient surrogates for accelerating cyclic adsorption simulations and optimization workflows.

candidates.title: Metal–Ligand Design of Co(II), Ni(II), Cu(II), and VO(II) Azo–Schiff Base Complexes: Structural Elucidation, DFT Insights, Promising Biological Activities and DNA Interactions
candidates.abstract: Abstract A new azo-Schiff base ligand, 2-ethoxy-4-(phenyldiazenyl)− 6-[(phenylimino)methyl]phenol (HL), was synthesized as a bidentate scaffold, giving rise to a new family of VO(II) (VOL), Co(II) (CoL), Ni(II) (NiL), and Cu(II) (CuL) complexes, then comprehensively characterized by CHN analysis, FT-IR, 1 H NMR, UV–Vis, magnetic characterization, TGA, mass spectroscopy, and powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD). From FT-IR data the shift of the azomethine ν(C=N) band from 1618 cm⁻ 1 in HL to 1633–1669 cm⁻ 1 in the complexes, together with the appearance of M–N and M–O vibrations, suggest bidentate coordination of the ligand through the azomethine nitrogen and deprotonated phenolic oxygen atoms. Magnetic susceptibility measurements gave μ eff values of 1.75, 3.92, 2.93, and 1.91 B.M. for VOL, CoL, NiL, and CuL, respectively, consistent with the proposed square-pyramidal geometry of VOL and distorted octahedral geometries of the CoL, NiL, and CuL complexes. CuL complex exhibit the smallest crystallite sizes (27.08 nm). Frontier molecular orbital analysis revealed that metal coordination reduced the energy gap of HL (ΔE = 5.93 eV). Among the complexes, VOL exhibited the lowest energy gap (ΔE = 2.78 eV) and higher softness (σ = 0.72 eV⁻ 1 ). The complexes displayed promising biological activities; CoL was the most active antimicrobial agent against Pseudomonas aeruginosa (AI = 183.3%) and Candida tropicalis (AI = 254.5%). NiL and VOL showed high radical scavenging efficiencies of 96.94% and 95.75%, and VOL exhibited the highest anti-inflammatory activity (IC₅₀ = 41.84 µg/mL), with CT-DNA binding affinity (K b = 2.28 × 10 5 M⁻ 1 ). Molecular docking against COX-2 enzyme showed that VOL complex displays the highest binding affinity (− 8.90 kcal/mol).

candidates.title: Federated multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for adaptive and lightweight secure protocol design in 6G networks
candidates.abstract: Abstract The move toward sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks introduces ultra-reliable low-latency communication and massive edge connectivity, but also enlarges the attack surface and demands security that is adaptive, lightweight, and decentralized. This paper presents a Federated Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (FMADRL) framework for adaptive secure-protocol selection, in which edge nodes learn local protection policies and share only model parameters. In this scheme, each edge node functions as an autonomous reinforcement learning agent that continuously observes local network conditions—including real-time threat indicators, computational resource availability, network latency, and remaining power—and selects an appropriate security protocol configuration through a trained deep Q-network. Local training proceeds via experience replay, and model parameters rather than raw data are periodically synchronized with a central aggregator to enable collective policy improvement across the federation. We formulate protocol selection as a Markov Decision Process that balances protection utility against computation and latency cost, and we evaluate a fully reproducible implementation in which every reported number is computed from runs. On a 20,000-sample evaluation set (50.5% attack steps; oracle reward ceiling 0.528), FMADRL reaches an average reward of 0.528—matching centralized DRL (0.528) without sharing raw data—while a static protocol reaches only 0.330. Because model poisoning is a central concern for security-focused federation, we integrate and test two Byzantine-robust aggregators: under a sign-flipping attack with 30% malicious agents, standard FedAvg collapses to a policy value of − 0.513, whereas Multi-Krum and Trimmed Mean hold ≈ 0.527. Gradient compression, evaluated by counting transmitted bytes, reduces per-round communication by up to 95.5% while retaining ≥ 99.5% of policy value. The model uses only 1,380 parameters, making edge inference inexpensive. Three principal findings emerge from this evaluation: the federated policy matches centralized DRL performance without sharing any raw network data; Byzantine-robust aggregation—Multi-Krum and Trimmed Mean—sustains near-optimal policy value even when 30% of agents are actively poisoning the federation, while standard FedAvg collapses to a negative reward under identical conditions; and aggressive gradient compression cuts per-round communication by 95.5% with negligible degradation in policy quality. These results collectively confirm that a decentralized, learning-based, Byzantine-aware framework is both practical and deployable as a security foundation for 6G communications.

candidates.title: LinearKnot: linear-time ensemble analysis of RNA density-2 pseudoknots under hierarchical folding
candidates.abstract: Motivation: A pseudoknot is an arrangement of crossing base pairs. Pseudoknots complicate structure prediction and calculations over possible structures (an ensemble). CParty sums structure weights for hierarchical pseudoknots that keep a supplied pseudoknot-free structure (scaffold). Its time is cubic in sequence length. Results: LinearKnot approximates CParty with beam pruning. It combines at most two partial structures in each step and keeps the highest-ranked candidates. At fixed beam width, hairpin length limit, and scaffold search limit, partition functions, minimum-free-energy (MFE) predictions, and representative {gamma}-centroid structures from base-pairing probabilities take linear time in sequence length. Loop profiles give probabilities for pairing and six unpaired loop types, including gaps between crossing stems (PseudoLoop). Window accessibility is the probability that a window is unpaired. For each RNA, we compared each base's distributions over pairing partners (including the unpaired state) and structural contexts with exact probabilities and averaged their total variation (TV) distances over bases unpaired in the scaffold. At width 200, the 90th percentiles of these RNA averages among 300-399-base RNAs were 0.0015 for pairing and 0.0017 for contexts. At width 100, LinearKnot completed partition functions for all 107 real RNAs through 29 kilobases. Under our settings, CParty completed RNAs up to about 1 kilobase and was faster on them. For the RNAcentral long non-coding RNA URS00023A4DB9 (29,106 nt), partition-function, pairing-probability, and MFE calculations at width 100 took about 7 minutes and 3.22 GiB. We compared free energy and pairing probabilities before and after each increase in beam width and local limits. These changes generally became smaller at larger widths. At width 200, the calculations for URS00023A4DB9 took about 20 minutes and 5.68 GiB. In rat telomerase RNA, a four-base window next to a pseudoknot was mostly unpaired as part of a PseudoLoop. A pseudoknot-free calculation with the same scaffold gave lower accessibility and placed the window mainly in a hairpin when unpaired. Availability and implementation: LinearKnot provides the linearknot command at https://github.com/TakumiOtagaki/LinearKnot. Experiment scripts and data are at https://github.com/TakumiOtagaki/LinearKnotExperiments.

candidates.title: Positive cooperativity enhances coupling of a second G protein to a GPCR dimer
candidates.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are cell surface integral membrane proteins that transduce environmental, hormonal and neurotransmitter molecular signals into intracellular responses. Here we studied a class D1 fungal receptor, Ste2, an obligate dimer that couples two G proteins per dimer and show that coupling of the second G protein has an 18-fold higher affinity than coupling of the first. The molecular mechanism uncovered suggests that coupling of the first G protein to one protomer stabilizes the adjacent protomer in an active conformation with a pre-formed G protein coupling site, thus increasing the affinity for coupling of the second G protein. Protomer-based stabilization of an adjacent protomer in a unique conformational state within a dimer may represent a general mechanism by which oligomerization alters GPCR pharmacology.

candidates.title: Translation uniformity and evolutionary conservation are associated with microprotein mass spectrometry detectability
candidates.abstract: Abstract Background Non-canonical open reading frames (ncORFs) encode a substantial, largely unexplored layer of the human proteome. The short microproteins they produce frequently escape detection by standard mass spectrometry (MS) workflows, creating a “dark proteome” that hampers gene annotation and functional characterisation. To address this, sequence-derived attributes were used to identify factors associated with MS repository detectability and to build an interpretable predictive framework that enables rational prioritisation of ncORFs for proteomic discovery. Results 7,097 ncORF sequences (99% <150 residues) were curated from the TransCODE Consortium, and labelled by PeptideAtlas peptide-level evidence as MS-detected ( n = 1,725) or undetected ( n = 5,372). An ensemble combining ESM-2 protein language model embeddings with logistic regression and nineteen biological features (ESM2-LR) achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.721 (SD 0.018, coefficient of variation 2.5% across ten independent runs). Model-agnostic SHAP and permutation importance analyses concordantly ranked cumulative in-frame ribosome footprint uniformity (CIF-HBP) as the strongest associated factor, followed by mammalian ORF-level evolutionary conservation (ORBLv_mammal) and genomic biotype. Predicted HLA class I-binding peptide density, which captures physicochemical properties overlapping with optimal LC-MS/MS analyte characteristics, was also positively associated with detectability. Late-fusion analysis demonstrated that ESM-2 embeddings and biological features contribute complementary predictive signals. Conclusions These findings indicate that sustained translation, purifying selection for ORF structural integrity, and favourable peptide physicochemistry converge to influence ncORF detectability. The ESM2-LR framework provides a reproducible, scalable tool to prioritise candidate microproteins for targeted MS validation, gene annotation, and the interpretation of disease-associated regulatory variants, subject to future external validation on independent datasets.

candidates.title: Tuning Supported Fe-Ag Catalysts for Selective Acetylene Hydrogenation: A Combined Experimental and Computational Study
candidates.abstract: Abstract The selective hydrogenation of acetylene is a key reaction step for purification in ethylene production, as trace amounts of acetylene can poison downstream polymerization catalysts. Industrial acetylene hydrogenation is currently performed almost exclusively using palladium-based catalysts, motivating the search for more abundant alternatives. In this study, supported Fe-Ag catalysts with different Fe:Ag ratios were synthesized and evaluated for the selective hydrogenation of acetylene under industrially relevant front-end conditions. The catalysts were characterized by XRD, N2-physisorption, TPR, XPS, STEM-EDX, ICP-OES and XRF, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs were used to investigate composition-dependent trends in adsorption energetics. Catalyst characterization revealed no evidence for the formation of an extended Fe-Ag alloy phase after air exposure. Instead, Fe- and Ag-rich domains were found to coexist in close nanoscale proximity providing a structural basis for considering possible local Fe-Ag interactions. Accordingly, the DFT calculations were performed on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs to investigate how the local chemical environment around adsorption sites affects the adsorption energetics of reaction intermediates. DFT calculations predict a gradual weakening of adsorption strength with increasing local Ag content, while the experimental catalyst series independently shows a decrease in ethane selectivity with increasing Ag loading. Under CO-containing front-end conditions, catalyst selectivity increased further due to competitive adsorption effects, while the influence of catalyst composition became less pronounced. The combined experimental and computational results indicate that changes in the local Fe-Ag environment influence adsorption energetics and may contribute to the composition-dependent catalytic behavior in acetylene hydrogenation. These findings provide design principles for the development of palladium-free hydrogenation catalysts based on earth-abundant metals.

candidates.title: R-PADE: Ranking-Guided Evolutionary Neural Architecture Search forMedical Image Segmentation
candidates.abstract: Neural architecture search (NAS) can automate medical image segmentation network design, but costly candidate evaluation limits the supervision available for evolutionary selection. Since replacement decisions depend on relative candidate quality, learning architecture preferences directly can provide guidance under constrained training budgets. In this paper, we propose Ranking-Aware Predictor-Assisted Differential Evolution (R-PADE) for U-Net-style architecture search. Specifically, a predictor trained with pairwise ranking supervision and contrastive regularization directly determines trial–target replacement in discrete differential evolution. Aggregated pairwise preferences prioritize candidates for proxy training, whose observations subsequently update the predictor. This connects evolutionary selection with selective candidate evaluation, reducing reliance on direct training for replacement decisions. Structured encoding and feasibility repair maintain valid architectures during the search. Experiments on CHAOS, BUSI, and ISIC demonstrate competitive segmentation performance with compact architectures. Compared with EU-Net, R-PADE reduces search GPU time by 35.6% while achieving higher Dice scores on CHAOS and BUSI. The ablation experiments compare the implemented predictor formulations and evaluate the contribution of contrastive regularization using matched search settings and proxy-evaluation budgets.

candidates.title: A Unified Conditional Flow for Motion Generation, Editing, and Intra-Structural Retargeting
candidates.abstract: Text-driven motion editing and intra-structural retargeting, where skeletons share topology but may differ in bone lengths and rest pose, are traditionally handled by fragmented pipelines with incompatible inputs and representations: editing relies on specialized generative steering, while retargeting is deferred to geometric post-processing. We present a unified conditional-flow framework that casts generation, semantic editing, and intra-structural retargeting as condition-modulated transport within one text- and skeleton-conditioned rectified-flow model. Under this formulation, editing changes the semantic condition while preserving skeletal structure, whereas retargeting changes the skeletal condition while preserving motion semantics. This makes FlowEdit-style transport a unified inference rule for motion manipulation rather than a task-specific editor. To instantiate this for articulated 3D motion, we develop a text- and skeleton-conditioned rectified-flow transformer. The model uses per-joint tokenization and explicit joint self-attention to capture spatial kinematic dependencies. We further inject text conditions at both joint and frame levels, while residual multi-condition classifier-free guidance balances text adherence and skeletal conformity. Experiments on SnapMoGen and a multi-character Mixamo subset show that one trained model supports text-to-motion generation, zero-shot editing, and zero-shot intra-structural retargeting without task-specific fine-tuning. This unified framework replaces separate pipelines with a single conditional motion transport model while keeping the same-topology retargeting scope explicit.

candidates.title: DynaConTalk: Wavelet-Constrained Diffusion for Long-Form and Controllable Holistic Co-Speech 3D Motion
candidates.abstract: Holistic co-speech animation is prone to averaging in both motion representation and speech conditioning. In coordinate-space diffusion, slow body posture, mid-frequency gesture strokes, and fast hand or facial details are entangled in one prediction target, often producing low-variance, over-smoothed motion. Meanwhile, fixed multimodal conditioning can let dense rhythmic and acoustic cues dominate sparse semantic cues, weakening rare content-specific gestures. We present DynaConTalk, a wavelet-constrained diffusion framework for long-form and controllable holistic co-speech motion generation. DynaConTalk performs diffusion in stationary wavelet transform (SWT) coefficient space, where temporally aligned bands separate coarse posture evolution, gesture strokes, and high-frequency expressive details. We further introduce dynamic proposal-consensus conditioning to adaptively balance rhythmic, acoustic, semantic, textual, and identity/activity cues according to the current speech context and denoising state. Finally, to ensure smooth transitions between windows and support flexible user control, we re-noise any reference signal - whether a keypose, a motion clip, or a short boundary condition - to match the current diffusion timestep before injecting it into the denoiser. This unified strategy allows seamless long-form generation, localized editing, and style-driven guidance to be handled within a single coherent process, without task-specific modules or post-hoc stitching. Experiments show that DynaConTalk improves gesture realism, facial accuracy, temporal continuity, and controllable editing over prior holistic co-speech generation methods. Code and data for this paper are at https://zhuyifeiabcd1.github.io/DynaConTalk/.

candidates.title: HERACLES for fast and accurate likelihood-based reconstruction of massive lineages
candidates.abstract: CRISPR-based lineage recording technologies can trace the ancestry of hundreds of thousands of cells, yet reconstructing accurate phylogenies at this scale remains computationally challenging. Likelihood-based methods employ explicit evolutionary models of CRISPR editing that improve tree accuracy but require computationally expensive searches over tree topologies, whereas distance-based alternatives scale efficiently but rely on distances that may not faithfully represent the editing process, introducing biases whose magnitude and direction are unknown. Here, we introduce HERACLES, which optimizes cell coordinates in hyperbolic space under a quartet-based composite likelihood of CRISPR editing. By recovering local branching structures directly from embedded distances, HERACLES guides continuous optimization with an explicit evolutionary model without repeatedly constructing and evaluating complete phylogenies. Across simulated benchmarks, HERACLES improves reconstruction accuracy over existing methods and scales to lineages containing 150,000 cells in about four hours on a single GPU. On experimental KP-tracer and PEtracer datasets, HERACLES reconstructs phylogenies consistent with independent anatomical annotations and temporal lineage markers. Its flexible likelihood framework also accommodates different recording mechanisms: incorporating sequential editing improves reconstruction of simulated DNA Typewriter lineages. Together, these results establish continuous optimization of local evolutionary relationships as a scalable and flexible approach to probabilistic lineage reconstruction.

candidates.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
candidates.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

candidates.title: Uniformly re-analysed public omics data and graded meta-analyses of exercise responses in humans and rodents
candidates.abstract: Hundreds of omics studies have profiled molecular responses to exercise, but they differ in species, tissue, protocol, sampling time and analysis pipeline, so their results are hard to combine. This dataset places the public evidence on a common scale. We screened GEO, PRIDE and Metabolomics Workbench for exercise studies in humans, mice and rats, defined exercise-control contrasts from sample-level metadata and uniformly re-analysed 1,037 contrasts from 448 independent study clusters, covering 20 tissue classes and seven molecular data types. For every contrast, the dataset provides moderated standardized effect sizes for each gene, protein, miRNA or metabolite and, for expression data, pathways. For 88 analysis units defined by tissue, exercise paradigm and molecular layer, it provides random-effects meta-analyses of every feature measured in at least three independent studies, with heterogeneity statistics, evidence classes assigned by pre-specified criteria and replication tests in two held-out training atlases. Curation records, code and a static query website are included. The data support look-up of molecules, new meta-analyses and planning and benchmarking of exercise studies.

candidates.title: TokenDial: Continuous Attribute Control for Text-to-Video Generation in Visual Dial Space
candidates.abstract: In video diffusion transformers, visual patch tokens maintain explicit correspondence to space and time. We hypothesize that their channel dimension can serve as a semantic control space, which we call Visual Dial Space V + . In this space, additive directions can be broadcast to the token stream to control appearance or motion attributes, enabling slider-style edits such as making a generated person look older or run faster. To verify the hypothesis, we present TokenDial , a framework for learning attribute directions in the proposed V + space. TokenDial keeps the pretrained video generator frozen and optimizes only additive directions. Rather than requiring paired edited videos, TokenDial supervises each direction through its induced effect on generated videos: the edited video should move along the desired attribute while the remaining content stays stable. The learned directions become reusable visual dials that support continuous appearance and motion control, explicit spatiotemporal localization, composition, and reuse across prompts, resolutions, and video lengths. Experiments and human studies show that TokenDial achieves stronger slider controllability and better content preservation than prior video editing and slider-based methods.
